slot.brief: Car on a level circular track; find minimum coefficient of friction for a given speed and radius, or maximum speed without skidding.

stem: A car of mass 1200 kg moves on a level circular track of radius 45 m at a constant speed of 54 km h^{-1}. The minimum coefficient of static friction required to prevent skidding is (Take g = 10 m s^{-2})

verdicts.working: Convert 54 km h⁻¹ to 15 m s⁻¹. For circular motion, μₛmg ≥ mv²/r, so μₛ,min = 15²/(45×10) = 0.50.

working:
v = 54 * (5/18) = 15 m s^{-1}. For a level circular track, static friction provides the centripetal force: μmg = mv^2/r. Hence μ = v^2/(rg) = 15^2/(45 * 10) = 225/450 = 0.50.

Independent check: Convert 54 km h⁻¹ to 15 m s⁻¹. For circular motion, μₛmg ≥ mv²/r, so μₛ,min = 15²/(45×10) = 0.50.
solution:
Convert the speed: $v=54\times\frac{5}{18}=15\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. Static friction provides the centripetal force:
$$\mu_s mg=\frac{mv^2}{r}\quad\Rightarrow\quad \mu_{s,\min}=\frac{15^2}{45\times10}=0.50.$$
